question: Should OpenClaw restore `PluginRuntime.channel.turn.*` as a deprecated compatibility alias for shipped third-party channel plugins, and what deprecation/removal policy should own it?
rationale: Root and scoped policy discourage convenience aliases, but explicitly allow public third-party API compatibility when a shipped contract broke existing plugins; automation cannot choose that API policy permanently.

options.title: Restore alias with deprecation
options.body: Merge the object-identical alias after rebase and keep `channel.inbound.*` as the documented canonical path with a named future-removal policy.

options.title: Reject runtime alias
options.body: Close or redirect this PR and require affected plugins to republish against `channel.inbound.*`, accepting that older installed plugins remain broken until upgraded.

options.title: Narrow to plugin releases
options.body: Patch specific affected plugin packages instead of core runtime, which fixes known packages but does not protect other third-party plugins compiled against the old runtime.

recommendation.title: Restore alias with deprecation
recommendation.body: Merge the object-identical alias after rebase and keep `channel.inbound.*` as the documented canonical path with a named future-removal policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The concrete removal provenance points to this handle, making them the best available owner for whether the old PluginRuntime name should stay deprecated-compatible.
